title: Candela pulse lab notes (scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
- Quick lab scratchpad to capture an odd cadence-shaped latency regression seen on 11/04 during integration testing with client-sim v2.
- Trying to reproduce and characterize: small, high-frequency bursts (200–800ms wide) separated by medium idle windows (5–12s).

Hypothesis:
- The runtime's batching heuristic + soft-priority lanes is over-coalescing during the trailing edge of bursts, producing a small cluster of large batches that inflates p95/p99 even though p50 stays fine.
- KV cache priming pattern interacts: cache miss storms at burst boundaries make CPU-side prep spike and delay batch dispatch.

Environment (testbed):
- Model: redwood-open-7b-v1 (float16 runtime; later runs include int8 quantized variant).
- Hardware: single A100-40GB instance (pinned) for controlled microbench; separate runs on 2xA100 for scale check.
- Runtime build: canary-2024-11-03 (batcher + soft-lane fixes not applied).
- Client sim: client-sim-v2 with Poisson+burst generator (config below).
- Telemetry: call-level traces + server-side timestamps + small pcap of request timing.

Client sim config used for main reproducer:
- baseline arrival: 5 qps background
- burst pattern: every 8s -> 600ms window, triangular envelope, peak 180 qps
- payload: short prompt (~12 tokens output target ~40 tokens)
- concurrency cap: 256

Key run notes (11/05):
- Warmup: 60s steady 5 qps to prime caches.
- Run length: 10 minutes (≈75 bursts).
- Observed behavior: p50 stable (~36ms), p95 and p99 spike only during burst trailing windows.

Representative latency summary (single A100, float16):
| Phase              | p50  | p95  | p99  | comments                           |
| ------------------ | ---- | ---- | ---- | ---------------------------------- |
| pre-burst (steady) | 36ms | 78ms | 140ms| warm cache, small batches         |
| burst peak         | 42ms | 220ms| 380ms| queueing + batching helps qps     |
| burst trailing     | 40ms | 410ms| 980ms| observed worst; big batches form |

Telemetry slices (what I pulled):
- trace-span ordering shows a 70–120ms CPU-side "prep" step for ~12% of requests that become p99s.
- KV cache logs: miss rate jumps from 18% -> 52% at burst start; miss handling correlates with CPU prep spikes.
- Batcher logs: batch sizes at trailing edge occasionally hit 48–64 (unexpected for these payloads) and dispatch latency has a bimodal distribution (fast paths vs coalesced large batch path).

Quick micro-experiments (iterated in the same session):
1) Disable soft-priority lanes (local flag): trailing p99 reduced from ~980ms -> ~310ms, p95 improved ~-160ms. Suggests lane heuristics are a factor.
2) Aggressive KV prefetch (client warm prefetch of cache keys before burst window): cache miss jump reduced to 26%, trailing p99 down to ~250ms.
3) Force max-batch-size=16 (override): more consistent tails but slightly lower peak throughput; p50 unchanged, p95 improved.
4) Quantized model (int8 run): overall latency up ~8–12ms p50 but p99s slightly lower when combined with max-batch-size=16 (makes sense: smaller memory pressure → less thrashing).

Notes on CPU/GPU utilization (observed with nvidia-smi + host top):
- During worst tail spikes GPU utilization stays high (~88–96%) but host CPU percent for "server-prep" threads spikes from 22% -> 76% for bursts.
- Indicates I/O/serialization + cache miss handling on CPU is creating dispatch delay.

Hypothesis refinement:
- Root cause is a two-way interaction: (A) KV cache miss storm at burst onset triggers CPU-bound work; (B) Batcher heuristic sees transient queue depth and decides to aggregate aggressively; aggregated batches then wait a bit for batch-filling window, causing a clump of high-latency requests at trailing edge.
- Secondary contributor: lightweight backoff timer jitter across dispatcher threads results in synchronized wake that amplifies coalescing.

Immediate mitigations to test next: (ordered)
- Short-term: set max-batch-size=16 and reduce batch-fill-window from 12ms -> 6ms (A/B test).
- Mid-term: improve KV cache priming (server side) to preempt miss storms for short prompts — try async prefetch on request headers.
- Longer-term: revise batcher heuristic to limit large-batch formation when CPU prep latency > threshold; add randomized dispatch jitter to break synchronization.

Checklist / next actions:
- [ ] Re-run reproducibility with canary that has soft-lane fix applied (PR #142) — compare p99 delta.
- [x] Validated that disabling soft lanes reduces tails (local flag).
- [ ] Evaluate server-side async prefetch prototype (prototype branch: bench/prefetch-2024).
- [ ] Add low-overhead host CPU profiling for "prep" thread to identify hotspots (mallocs? protobuf parse?).
- [ ] Schedule pair session with batcher owner (Mira) and cache owner (Noah) next week (suggested: 11/13).

Open questions / weirdness to follow up:
- Why does the cache miss spike at burst boundaries even with steady 5 qps warmup? Are prefix tokens varying enough that hot key set thrashes? (need per-token key distribution).
- Could client timing jitter be causing synchronization across dispatcher threads? Need event-level ordering to confirm.
- When we ran 2x A100 the trailing p99 still existed but magnitude reduced ~30% — suggests partial mitigation from extra headroom but not root-cause removal.

Notes-to-self:
- Keep this file minimal; copy polished summary to shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/bench-reports after we have A/B results.
- Attach traces + small sample pcap to Linear ticket RED-2417.

End of scratchpad — Felipe
